hero.headline: Judge orders Trump to respond to fraud claims in IRS lawsuit settlement
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered President Trump to respond to allegations that a settlement in his lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service constitutes fraud. The judge is scrutinizing whether an agreement that created a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund was conducted improperly.

The case involves Trump's lawsuit demanding $10 billion from the IRS. As part of settlement negotiations between Trump's legal team and the tax agency, an anti-weaponization fund worth $1.8 billion was established. The judge's decision to reopen parts of the case signals concerns about the legitimacy and structure of this financial arrangement.

According to court documents, the judge characterized the allegations as serious, prompting the order for Trump to provide detailed answers about the settlement. Specifically, the president must address questions about whether the fund was created fraudulently and explain how the settlement was negotiated and structured.

The judge's order represents a significant development in the ongoing legal dispute between the president and the IRS. The decision to require Trump's response suggests the court has concerns about the validity of the agreement and wants a full accounting of how the deal was arranged.

Legal experts note that fraud allegations in federal court require careful examination of the facts and circumstances surrounding any agreement. The specifics of how the anti-weaponization fund was created and what it was intended to accomplish appear central to the judge's inquiry.

The court has set a timeline for Trump's required response. His legal team will need to provide documentation and explanations detailing the negotiation process and the reasoning behind the fund's structure. This level of scrutiny indicates the judge is taking the fraud allegations seriously enough to warrant a thorough examination of the settlement agreement.

Trump faces multiple court proceedings on various matters, and the IRS lawsuit represents one of several ongoing legal battles involving the president and federal agencies. Each case involves complex legal questions and significant financial stakes.

The reopening of this lawsuit and the demand for answers about the settlement adds another layer to Trump's legal challenges. How the president's legal team responds to the judge's questions could influence the outcome of this dispute with the IRS and potentially affect how courts view other settlement agreements involving the administration.

The case highlights ongoing questions about the settlement process and how billion-dollar funds are created and managed through legal agreements. The judge's insistence on answers about whether fraud occurred underscores the importance courts place on transparency and proper procedures in major financial arrangements involving the government and the president.

cards.headline: Trump Delays Final Decision on Iran Nuclear Deal
cards.teaser: The president said he would make a determination soon on whether to proceed with an agreement to end hostilities.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers to discuss a potential agreement with Iran after U.S. officials confirmed that both nations had agreed on a framework for a deal. No agreement was announced following the meeting.

The president has indicated he will make a final determination on whether to proceed with the deal in the coming days. The situation reflects the challenges previous U.S. administrations have faced in dealing with Iran as an adversary.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Tells Asian Allies to Increase Military Spending
cards.teaser: At a Singapore security conference, Pete Hegseth said countries must do more to receive priority US assistance.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth addressed Asian military leaders at a security summit in Singapore, emphasizing that the US remains committed to the region while calling on allies to strengthen their defense capabilities. He indicated that countries boosting their military spending would receive prioritized access to US military assistance and arms deals.

Hegseth's remarks came following President Trump's recent visit to China. The defense secretary outlined a need for a coordinated regional defense strategy to address China's growing military presence in Asia.

cards.headline: Defense secretary disputes claim Iran war delayed Taiwan arms sale
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pushed back Saturday against claims that military operations related to the Iran conflict have delayed a major weapons package to Taiwan.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the previous week that the U.S. was postponing a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Cao attributed the delay to the need to preserve America's shrinking munitions stockpiles as the military conducts operations across multiple regions.

Hegseth rejected that explanation, signaling disagreement within the defense establishment over how the Iran war is affecting military readiness and U.S. commitments to allied nations.

The disagreement reflects broader tensions over resource allocation. Military officials have previously expressed concerns about weapons supplies as the Pentagon maintains operations in the Middle East while providing arms to partners like Taiwan.

Taiwan has sought to modernize its military capabilities amid regional security concerns and regularly purchases American weapons as part of its defense strategy. The $14 billion package represents one of the largest proposed arms sales and would include multiple weapons systems.

The Pentagon has not disclosed additional details about the status of the Taiwan sale or the expected duration of any delay.

Both Hegseth and Cao serve as Trump administration appointees in senior defense positions. Their public disagreement highlights differing views on how the Iran war impacts U.S. military commitments and readiness.

The conflict has already taken a toll on American forces. In a recent incident, six service members were killed in a refueling tanker crash while conducting operations related to the Iran war. At a Dover Air Force Base transfer ceremony for the fallen troops, Hegseth told reporters he had spoken with family members of all six service members killed.

According to Hegseth, families expressed determination to continue military efforts. "What I heard through tears, through hugs, through strength and through unbreakable resolve, was the same from family after family," he said. "They said, 'Finish this. Honor their sacrifice. Do not waver. Do not stop until the job is done.'"

However, Charles Simmons, the father of one of the fallen service members, contradicted this account. Simmons told NBC News he did not discuss continuing the Iran war with Hegseth or President Trump at Dover. "I can't speak for the other families. When he spoke to me, that was not something we talked about," Simmons said.

Simmons expressed uncertainty about the necessity of the conflict. "I just certainly hope the decisions being made are necessary," he said he told Hegseth.

Other family members have also questioned the war. Stephan Douglas, a cousin of one of the fallen service members, said the conflict was unnecessary. "We didn't need to be in this war," Douglas stated.

The Iran war has had wider economic effects, with U.S. inflation rising at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven significantly by higher energy prices.

cards.headline: Proposed federal rules would allow grants to be canceled anytime, make peer review optional
cards.body:
The federal government has proposed new rules for research funding that would allow grants to be terminated at any time and make peer review optional. Political staff would gain authority to screen grant applications for forbidden topics.

The proposed changes represent a major shift in how federal research funding operates. Under current practices, peer review by subject matter experts forms the foundation of grant approval processes. The new rules would make this practice discretionary rather than required.

Political appointees would review grant applications to identify research on topics deemed off limits, though the proposal does not specify which subjects would fall under restrictions. This screening process would occur alongside or instead of traditional scientific evaluation.

The cancellation provision would give funding agencies power to end grants after they have been awarded and research has begun. Existing grant agreements typically include specific terms and timelines that provide stability for research projects, which often span multiple years.

Research institutions and scientists rely on grant funding to conduct studies, pay staff, and maintain laboratories. Federal agencies including the National Institutes of Health and National Science Foundation award billions of dollars in competitive grants each year. These funds support work ranging from basic science to applied research in medicine, technology, and other fields.

The proposal applies to future grant awards. How it would interact with existing grant agreements remains unaddressed in the available information about the rules.

The shift toward optional peer review and expanded political oversight marks a departure from long standing practices in federal research funding. Scientific organizations have traditionally advocated for peer review as a way to ensure research quality and prevent political interference in scientific decision making.

The proposed rules do not indicate when they might take effect or what process would govern grant cancellations if the changes are adopted. Federal agencies typically accept public comment on proposed rule changes before finalizing them.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test, Threatening NASA Moon Mission Timeline
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during a static fire test on Thursday evening, destroying the launch facility and potentially derailing NASA's ambitious plans to return humans to the Moon.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during the scheduled hotfire test at Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 36. A massive fireball engulfed the launchpad, and the blast was so powerful that residents reported feeling shockwaves across Florida's space coast. An orange sky was visible as far south as Fort Pierce, roughly 115 miles away, while people in South Carolina hundreds of miles north reported seeing the glow from the explosion.

Blue Origin confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured. The company described the incident as "an anomaly" but has not yet disclosed the root cause or provided a revised timeline for its programs.

The timing of the explosion creates significant challenges for NASA's Artemis program. Just one day before the test, NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned lunar missions this year to begin construction of NASA's $20 billion Moon base. The New Glenn rocket is central to Blue Origin's strategy to support these missions, as it is the vehicle the company intends to use to launch landers to the Moon, including those that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface.

Blue Origin is also competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028, which would mark the first crewed lunar landing since 1972. Artemis III, scheduled for 2027, is set to test both Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which will transport astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote on social media. NASA pledged to work with partners to support a thorough investigation and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

This explosion represents the latest setback for Blue Origin as it attempts to establish itself as a reliable government contractor. Last month, a payload from the New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, and the FAA temporarily grounded the rocket. The company had only recently been cleared to return to flight operations before Thursday's test.

The Federal Aviation Administration has not yet indicated whether the explosion will trigger another investigation. The extent of the damage to the launch facility and the findings of Blue Origin's investigation will determine how significantly the company's participation in NASA's lunar missions will be delayed.

cards.headline: SpaceX Awarded $4.16 Billion Space Force Contract for Satellite Network
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force has awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to build a satellite network designed to track airborne targets.
cards.body:
SpaceX won a $4.16 billion contract from the U.S. Space Force to build missile-tracking satellites for the Space Based Airborne Target Indicator program, also known as "Golden Dome." The sensor-equipped satellites will detect and track airborne targets from space-based platforms.

The contract represents a significant portion of SpaceX's government revenue. According to the company's IPO filing, government contracts already generated one-fifth of SpaceX's 2025 revenue, underscoring the company's growing importance to U.S. defense capabilities.

hero.headline: Ebola Outbreak Overwhelms Remote Mining Town in Africa
hero.body:
A remote gold mining town in Africa has become the center of a spiraling Ebola outbreak, with medical workers struggling to contain a surge of deaths and infections.

Declan Walsh, an Africa correspondent, visited an Ebola ward where both adults and children were receiving treatment. Someone had recently died of the disease in the facility he observed. The ward is part of a medical response attempting to address the outbreak in the region.

The town under siege is described as remote and centered around gold mining. Medical staff are facing difficulties as they work to beat back the rising number of cases. The outbreak has produced both fatalities and new infections that continue to strain local healthcare capacity.

The specific location of the outbreak and the total number of cases were not disclosed in available reports. The situation represents a public health crisis in a region with limited medical infrastructure. Ebola is a severe viral disease that spreads through contact with bodily fluids and often proves fatal without prompt treatment.

Healthcare workers in the affected area are dealing with patients across age groups, including children, while working under conditions that reflect the challenges of operating in a remote mining community. The recent death observed during the ward visit underscores the ongoing threat the virus poses to the local population.

The outbreak has drawn international attention as medical personnel work to prevent further spread of the disease. Ebola outbreaks typically require intensive containment efforts, including isolation of patients, contact tracing, and protective equipment for healthcare workers. The remote nature of the affected town adds logistical complications to the response effort.

cards.headline: Four More Miners Rescued After 10 Days Trapped in Flooded Laos Cave
cards.teaser: Rescuers freed four of seven villagers who entered narrow tunnels searching for gold, with two still missing.
cards.body:
Four men have been rescued from a flooded cave in Laos after being trapped for 10 days. The miners entered narrow tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold. Divers conducted the hazardous rescue operation, navigating through muddy water and sharp rocks to reach the trapped men.

Two of the original seven villagers remain missing. Rescue teams continue their efforts to locate them, working to drain water from the cave system and navigate around collapse hazards in the flooded passages.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Tells Asian Allies to Increase Military Spending
cards.teaser: At a Singapore security conference, Pete Hegseth said countries must do more to receive priority US assistance.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth addressed Asian military leaders at a security summit in Singapore, emphasizing that the US remains committed to the region while calling on allies to strengthen their defense capabilities. cards.headline: Japan Visa Rules Force Foreign Business Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New immigration restrictions under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting entrepreneurs who have established businesses in the country.
cards.body:
New visa rules in Japan are forcing some foreign business owners to leave the country, even after they have put down roots there. The restrictions are part of an immigration crackdown under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

Curry shop owners are among those caught in the tightened visa requirements. The policy changes affect foreign entrepreneurs who have established businesses in Japan and built lives in the country. The immigration measures represent a shift in how Japan handles foreign business ownership and residency.

cards.headline: Vietnam Leader Says Better China Relations Can Help Regional Security
cards.teaser: Vietnam's top leader discussed the benefits of improved ties with China amid broader concerns about superpower conflict in Asia.
cards.body:
Vietnam's leader said that better relations with China can help promote regional peace and security. The statement came as Asian countries seek responsible commitment from major powers in the region.

The Vietnamese president warned about the risks of superpower conflict in Asia. His comments were made as an Asia defense summit opened in Singapore, where concerns about China and doubts about US priorities topped the agenda. Vietnam is positioning itself amid tensions between major powers in the Asia Pacific region.

cards.headline: Concerts by Ye and Travis Scott Canceled in Italy Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities canceled the events to ensure public order and safety after objections from Jewish leaders.
cards.body:
Concerts by Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, and Travis Scott were canceled in Italy over public safety concerns. Italian authorities determined that proceeding with the events posed risks and made the cancellations to ensure public order and safety.

Jewish leaders had objected to Ye's concert due to his history of antisemitic remarks. Security concerns ultimately led officials to cancel both performances.

cards.headline: No deal announced after Trump meets advisers on Iran framework
cards.teaser: President Trump met with advisers but did not announce a final determination after US and Iranian officials confirmed they had agreed on a framework.
cards.body:
President Trump convened with his advisers following confirmation that the United States and Iran had reached a framework agreement. However, no final deal was announced at the conclusion of the meeting.

Trump had indicated he would make a definitive decision on Iran policy during the discussions with his team. The framework represents a significant development in negotiations between the two nations, though the president has yet to reveal his next steps regarding a comprehensive agreement.

cards.headline: Trump's doctor says president is in excellent health after checkup
cards.teaser: President Trump's physician declared him in excellent health and fully fit to serve following a medical examination at Walter Reed.
cards.body:
President Trump's doctor has declared him to be in excellent health and fully fit to carry out his duties following his latest annual physical examination. The White House released the results of the medical checkup.

During the examination, Trump's doctor recommended that the president lose weight and exercise more as part of maintaining his health going forward.

cards.headline: Liverpool fires head coach Arne Slot one year after title win
cards.teaser: Liverpool dismissed Arne Slot after two seasons, with Andoni Iraola emerging as the leading candidate to replace him.
cards.body:
Liverpool has sacked head coach Arne Slot following two seasons in charge. The decision comes roughly a year after the team won the Premier League title under his management.

Andoni Iraola is the leading candidate to succeed Slot as Liverpool's next head coach.

cards.headline: 15-year-old girl dies after swimming at beach
cards.teaser: Chiedza Nyanjowa died following an incident while swimming, her family remembering her as a bubbly person with a kind spirit.
cards.body:
A 15-year-old girl died after swimming at a beach. Chiedza Nyanjowa's family released a statement describing her character and the loss they are experiencing.

Her family said Chiedza was a bubbly person with a kind spirit. They shared their memories of her following the incident that took her life while she was swimming.

cards.headline: Palace received Prince Andrew's controversial envoy emails six years ago
cards.teaser: The Royal Household was given thousands of emails about the former prince's financial dealings in 2020.
cards.body: The Royal Household received thousands of emails concerning Prince Andrew's financial dealings in 2020. The correspondence relates to the former prince's activities as a royal envoy before he stepped back from public duties.

cards.headline: Heathrow train services resume after pipe burst caused delays
cards.teaser: All train services to and from Heathrow Airport were cancelled following a burst pipe but have now reopened.
cards.body:
Train lines serving Heathrow Airport have reopened after a burst pipe forced the cancellation of all services. The incident caused major delays for travelers using the airport.

All train services to and from Heathrow were initially suspended due to the pipe burst. Operations have since resumed, restoring rail connections to the airport.

cards.headline: Dell Stock Hits All-Time High on AI Server Demand
cards.teaser: Dell stock surged to a record high after the company reported strong quarterly results driven by demand for AI servers.
cards.body:
Dell shares soared to an all-time high following a blowout quarterly report that exceeded expectations. The rally was fueled by robust demand for the company's AI servers and infrastructure products during the ongoing artificial intelligence boom.

The stock surge added $34 billion to founder Michael Dell's personal fortune in a single day, the company's best trading day ever. Analysts described the quarter as setting up what could be an important week for AI-related technology stocks.

cards.headline: Replimune Gets Third Chance at FDA Approval After White House Involvement
cards.teaser: Replimune will resubmit its twice-rejected cancer drug for FDA approval following what the company described as productive talks with regulators.
cards.body:
Replimune plans to resubmit its melanoma treatment for FDA approval after the drug was rejected twice previously. The biotech company announced it will take a third attempt at gaining regulatory approval following discussions with the FDA.

The company's stock shot up 80 percent on news of the resubmission plans. Reports indicate White House intervention played a role in giving the drug another opportunity for review, though the FDA has stood by its past rejection decisions.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Detained
cards.teaser: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after an unruly passenger was detained following an in-flight incident.
cards.body:
United Airlines Flight 2005 was diverted to Dane County Regional Airport in Madison, Wisconsin, after crew members detained a disruptive passenger. The flight had departed from Chicago and was bound for Minneapolis when the incident occurred.

Audio recordings indicate the diversion may have involved an attempted cockpit breach. The passenger was taken into custody after the plane landed safely in Madison. The aircraft was traveling as a standard domestic route when the disruption forced the unscheduled landing.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Industry Advances in Drug Development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference, highlighting the country's growing pharmaceutical capabilities.
cards.body:
Chinese researchers are presenting clinical trial results at an international oncology conference in Chicago, drawing increased attention to the country's growing biotech sector. The presentations highlight China's expanding drug development capabilities and clinical trial infrastructure.

The surge in China's biotechnology advancement is prompting concern among U.S. industry observers about the country's competitive position in pharmaceutical development.

cards.headline: Southwest Airlines Revises Extra Seat Policy for Plus-Size Passengers
cards.teaser: Southwest Airlines has updated its policy regarding extra seat accommodations for plus-size passengers after facing months of backlash.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines changed its seating policy for passengers who require extra space after the previous rule drew criticism. The airline implemented the update following four months of negative feedback from customers and advocacy groups.

The policy revision modifies how the airline handles requests and accommodations for passengers who need additional seating. Southwest had faced pushback over what critics described as unclear or burdensome requirements under the previous policy framework.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts before planned IPO
cards.teaser: The contracts come as SpaceX disclosed that government work accounted for one fifth of its 2025 revenue.
cards.body:
SpaceX has been awarded $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, with the timing coming as the company prepares for its initial public offering.

According to SpaceX's IPO filing, government contracts accounted for one-fifth of the company's 2025 revenue. These new Space Force awards will further strengthen the company's government revenue stream ahead of its public debut.

cards.headline: DuckDuckGo search traffic increases as users respond to Google AI changes
cards.teaser: The privacy focused search engine saw rising traffic and installations after Google introduced AI features across its search platform.
cards.body:
DuckDuckGo has seen a surge in search traffic and app installations following Google's decision to integrate artificial intelligence features into its search engine. The shift occurred after Google announced an AI-focused overhaul at its developer conference.

The alternative search engine appeals to users seeking traditional search results without AI-generated content. As Google prioritizes AI integration across its platform, DuckDuckGo's option for conventional search functionality has attracted users looking for a different approach.

cards.headline: Programmers increasingly rely on AI coding tools despite quality concerns
cards.teaser: Some software developers now refuse to work without AI assistance, though researchers warn the tools may not improve code quality.
cards.body:
A growing number of programmers are using AI tools to write code faster, with some refusing to work without the technology. Researchers have raised concerns that while AI speeds up code production, it may not result in better quality software.

The tools help coders generate code more quickly than traditional methods. However, the potential gap between speed and quality could create future problems for developers who have become dependent on AI assistance.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes state based coal ash monitoring in place of federal standards
cards.teaser: Environmental groups gathered to oppose proposed changes that would let states handle coal ash oversight and bypass national requirements.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed allowing states to take over monitoring and enforcement of coal ash regulations. The changes would let states bypass national standards for handling coal ash, the waste product from coal fired power plants.

Environmental organizations turned out in large numbers to oppose the proposed rollbacks. The administration's plan would shift responsibility for coal ash oversight from federal to state authorities.

cards.headline: Study identifies liver sensors that may help pigeons navigate using magnetic fields
cards.teaser: Researchers report that homing pigeons appear to use magnetic sensors located in their livers for navigation.
cards.body:
Pigeons may navigate using magnetic field sensors in their livers, according to a new study. The research suggests the birds rely on these liver based sensors to detect Earth's magnetic field, particularly when traveling long distances on cloudy days.

The findings offer a potential explanation for how homing pigeons find their way home across vast distances. Some scientists in the field have expressed skepticism about the liver navigation mechanism, indicating the research remains subject to debate.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad practices draws support from company founders
cards.teaser: A court decision regarding Google's advertising business has prompted startup founders to renew criticism of how platforms use trademarked keywords.
cards.body:
An Indian court has issued a ruling on Google's advertising practices that has drawn support from company founders. The decision focuses on how the platform handles trademarked keywords in its ad system.

The ruling could prompt digital platforms to reconsider their policies around trademarked keywords. It highlights the ongoing tension between advertising practices and trademark protections in the digital space.

hero.headline: Liverpool fires head coach Arne Slot after two seasons
hero.body:
Liverpool has sacked head coach Arne Slot with immediate effect following a disappointing title defense in his second season. The club has confirmed the dismissal and is actively pursuing Andoni Iraola as his replacement.

Slot's departure comes after a troubled campaign that saw Liverpool win just 45 points from their final 33 matches. The season was marked by significant challenges, including the death of player Diogo Jota and 19 defeats across all competitions. Despite Liverpool's reluctance in making the decision, a club review prompted the change.

The contrast with Slot's first season is stark. In his debut campaign, the Dutch manager guided Liverpool to the Premier League title, a remarkable achievement that demonstrated his tactical acumen and ability to motivate the squad. However, the team's collapse in the title defense proved difficult to overcome, with the club ultimately finishing fifth in the league standings.

Several factors contributed to this season's struggles. Key players suffered injuries throughout the campaign, disrupting team continuity and forcing adjustments to the squad's setup. Additionally, star player Mohamed Salah experienced a decline in form, which impacted the team's attacking output. The tragic loss of Diogo Jota also overshadowed the season, affecting the squad's morale and focus.

Iraola has emerged as the leading candidate to take the position. The club is expected to move quickly in appointing a successor, though no official timeline has been announced. Iraola's name is being discussed prominently across major sports outlets as the favorite to fill the vacancy.

Slot's sacking represents a notable shift in Liverpool's approach to management. The club's decision reflects a pattern among elite Premier League teams to make swift changes when performance falls short of expectations. However, supporters and analysts have expressed mixed views on the decision. Some argue that Slot deserved more time given the obstacles the team faced, particularly the loss of Jota and persistent injury issues.

The club stated the decision was made with great reluctance following a thorough review of the season. Liverpool's ownership and leadership felt compelled to act despite recognizing the difficult circumstances that hampered the team's performance.

This managerial change marks a critical moment for Liverpool as it seeks to return to competing for major honors. The club must now stabilize its coaching situation and establish a clear direction for the team moving forward. How the club navigates this transition will likely shape Liverpool's ambitions for the upcoming season and beyond.

cards.headline: Golden Knights to face Hurricanes in Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights will play the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2026 Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2026 Stanley Cup Final. The Hurricanes advanced by defeating Montreal, ending a 20-year drought since their last Cup final appearance in 2006. Head coach Rod Brind'Amour's team broke through a years-long Eastern Conference final barrier to reach this championship series.

The matchup sets up a battle between the Western Conference champion Golden Knights and the Hurricanes, who are seeking their first Stanley Cup title in two decades. The series will begin in the coming days, with games scheduled in Las Vegas where ticket demand has driven prices to high levels.

cards.headline: Former Indiana quarterback admits betting nearly $90,000 during college career
cards.teaser: Brendan Sorsby acknowledged placing at least 40 bets on Indiana football while he was a quarterback for the team.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby confirmed he wagered at least $90,000 during his college career, including placing at least 40 bets on Indiana football games while serving as the team's quarterback. Law enforcement flagged his gambling activity to the NCAA.

Sorsby now plays for the New England Patriots. His admission comes as the NCAA investigates gambling violations among college athletes, with potential implications for enforcement policies.

cards.headline: Budapest police investigating fan violence before Champions League final
cards.teaser: Police in Budapest made arrests and are reviewing video footage after supporters fought before the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Police in Budapest have arrested multiple people following a brawl between supporters ahead of Saturday's Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris St-Germain. Authorities are reviewing CCTV footage to identify additional participants in the violence.

The match takes place in Budapest, where security has been a concern around the championship game between the two clubs.

cards.headline: Canada names Alphonso Davies to World Cup squad
cards.teaser: Head coach Jesse Marsch selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for what he called the best Canada squad ever assembled.
cards.body:
Canada head coach Jesse Marsch has selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for the national team's World Cup squad this summer. Marsch believes this is the strongest squad Canada has ever assembled for the tournament.

Davies brings elite-level experience from his club career at one of Europe's top teams to represent Canada on the global stage.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho's relationship with Vinicius Junior in focus at Real Madrid
cards.teaser: Mourinho's handling of Brazil forward Vinicius Junior will be closely watched during his second stint managing Real Madrid.
cards.body: Jose Mourinho has returned to Real Madrid for a second spell as manager. His appointment has drawn significant attention to how he will manage his relationship with Brazil forward Vinicius Junior, making it one of the most closely watched aspects of his return to the club.

cards.headline: Tactics Arsenal could use to win Champions League final
cards.teaser: BBC Sport's tactics correspondent analyzed how Arsenal can defeat Paris St-Germain in the Champions League final.
cards.body:
BBC Sport's tactics correspondent Umir Irfan has analysed the strategies Arsenal might deploy to beat Paris St-Germain in Saturday's Champions League final in Budapest.

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start the match, having recovered from a groin injury that kept him sidelined for more than two months.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who helped shape Star Wars and other landmark films of the 1970s, died on Wednesday at her home in Rancho Mirage, California, following a battle with metastatic cancer. She was 80. Lucasfilm posted a statement expressing deep sadness over her passing.

Lucas was one of three editors to share an Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film. Her work helped define the visual rhythm and pacing of George Lucas's space epic, which became one of the most influential films in cinema history.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited several iconic films of the 1970s, including Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver. Her editorial contributions during this period helped establish her as one of the era's most respected film editors.

Lucas was formerly married to George Lucas, the creator and director of Star Wars. The couple divorced after the completion of the original trilogy.

Lucasfilm's statement acknowledged her contributions to the studio's history and expressed condolences following her death. The statement noted that the company was deeply saddened by the loss.

Lucas died in Rancho Mirage, a desert city in Riverside County, California, where she had been living. Her death followed an extended battle with metastatic cancer, a form of cancer that spreads from its original site to other parts of the body.

The film industry has lost one of its pioneering editors whose work on Star Wars and other films of the 1970s left a lasting impact on cinema. Her editorial vision helped create some of the most memorable sequences in American film history.

cards.headline: Arsenal to Face PSG in UEFA Champions League Final
cards.teaser: Arsenal F.C. and Paris Saint-Germain F.C. will compete for the European Champion Clubs Cup on Saturday.
cards.body:
The 2026 UEFA Champions League Final takes place on Saturday, May 30, at Puskas Arena in Budapest, Hungary. Arsenal F.C. will face Paris Saint-Germain F.C., with The Killers headlining the pre-match kickoff show. The winner will claim the European Champion Clubs Cup, one of soccer's most prestigious trophies.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start the final after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for more than two months. Ahead of the match, Arsenal players including Leandro Trossard, Declan Rice, and Eberechi Eze reflected on what winning the trophy would mean to the club.

cards.headline: Dmitry Bivol Defends Three Light Heavyweight Titles Against Michael Eifert
cards.teaser: Russian boxer Dmitry Bivol puts his IBF, WBA and WBO light heavyweight championship belts on the line in a 12-round bout.
cards.body:
Dmitry Bivol will defend his IBF, WBA and WBO light heavyweight titles against German boxer Michael Eifert in a championship bout. The 12-round match features Bivol's three championship belts at stake.

The contest will determine whether Bivol retains all three titles or if Eifert claims the championships. The fight represents a significant moment in the light heavyweight division.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old music mogul was admitted to a New York City hospital following a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening after experiencing a respiratory issue. The music executive is 94 years old.

Davis has been a prominent figure in the music industry for decades, working with numerous major artists throughout his career. He was admitted to a New York hospital for treatment of the respiratory condition.

cards.headline: Multiple Artists Drop Out of Trump-Backed Freedom 250 Concert
cards.teaser: Over half of performers scheduled for the Great American State Fair concerts have withdrawn from the Trump-backed events.
cards.body:
At least seven of the nine featured musical acts scheduled to perform at the Trump administration's Freedom 250 concert series have withdrawn from the event. The concerts were organized to commemorate the United States' 250th anniversary on July 4, with performances planned for the National Mall in Washington, D.C.

Bret Michaels became the latest artist to exit the lineup on Friday, citing threats and a deteriorating atmosphere surrounding the event. The withdrawals occurred within 48 hours of the initial lineup announcement, significantly impacting the roster for the celebration.

cards.headline: Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe Says Sewing Helped Her Survive Iranian Prison
cards.teaser: The British-Iranian woman told an audience that creativity provided a psychological escape during her imprisonment.
cards.body:
Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe spoke to an audience about her experience in Iranian prison, describing how sewing became a lifeline during her detention. She told attendees that creativity provided a quick psychological exit when freedom was restricted.

Zaghari-Ratcliffe credited the creative activity with helping her cope with the mental challenges of imprisonment. She explained that engaging in sewing allowed her to mentally escape the confines of her situation.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Reflects on Family Life During Beatles Fame
cards.teaser: The musician discussed how his family kept him grounded during the height of Beatlemania.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney shared details about a turning point during the Beatles' rise to fame and how he managed life in the spotlight. The musician reflected on his experiences during the band's peak popularity period.

McCartney credited his family with helping him stay grounded during Beatlemania, when the band's fame reached unprecedented levels. He described how his family relationships provided stability while navigating the intense public attention that came with being a member of the Beatles.

hero.headline: Defense secretary disputes claim Iran war delayed Taiwan arms sale
hero.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pushed back Saturday against claims that military operations related to the Iran conflict have delayed a major weapons package to Taiwan.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators the previous week that the U.S. was postponing a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Cao attributed the delay to the need to preserve America's shrinking munitions stockpiles as the military conducts operations across multiple regions.

Hegseth rejected that explanation, signaling disagreement within the defense establishment over how the Iran war is affecting military readiness and U.S. commitments to allied nations.

The disagreement reflects broader tensions over resource allocation. Military officials have previously expressed concerns about weapons supplies as the Pentagon maintains operations in the Middle East while providing arms to partners like Taiwan.

Taiwan has sought to modernize its military capabilities amid regional security concerns and regularly purchases American weapons as part of its defense strategy. The $14 billion package represents one of the largest proposed arms sales and would include multiple weapons systems.

The Pentagon has not disclosed additional details about the status of the Taiwan sale or the expected duration of any delay.

Both Hegseth and Cao serve as Trump administration appointees in senior defense positions. Their public disagreement highlights differing views on how the Iran war impacts U.S. military commitments and readiness.

The conflict has already taken a toll on American forces. In a recent incident, six service members were killed in a refueling tanker crash while conducting operations related to the Iran war. At a Dover Air Force Base transfer ceremony for the fallen troops, Hegseth told reporters he had spoken with family members of all six service members killed.

According to Hegseth, families expressed determination to continue military efforts. "What I heard through tears, through hugs, through strength and through unbreakable resolve, was the same from family after family," he said. "They said, 'Finish this. Honor their sacrifice. Do not waver. Do not stop until the job is done.'"

However, Charles Simmons, the father of one of the fallen service members, contradicted this account. Simmons told NBC News he did not discuss continuing the Iran war with Hegseth or President Trump at Dover. "I can't speak for the other families. When he spoke to me, that was not something we talked about," Simmons said.

Simmons expressed uncertainty about the necessity of the conflict. "I just certainly hope the decisions being made are necessary," he said he told Hegseth.

Other family members have also questioned the war. Stephan Douglas, a cousin of one of the fallen service members, said the conflict was unnecessary. "We didn't need to be in this war," Douglas stated.

The Iran war has had wider economic effects, with U.S. inflation rising at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven significantly by higher energy prices.

cards.headline: Attorney General Bondi testified in Epstein investigation
cards.teaser: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi gave testimony in the ongoing Epstein investigation this week.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before the House Oversight and Reform Committee about the Justice Department's handling of Epstein files during her tenure. Bondi defended the DOJ's management of the case, though she acknowledged "redaction errors" in the files. She told lawmakers that she delegated oversight of the effort to Todd Blanche, her former deputy attorney general who is now acting attorney general.

Democratic lawmakers noted that Bondi declined to answer questions about Donald Trump's involvement in the release of the files. The testimony came about a month after the current attorney general was removed from office by President Trump.

cards.headline: Navy to power Norfolk base with nuclear aircraft carrier
cards.teaser: The Navy plans to use a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier to supply electricity to its largest base.
cards.body:
The U.S. Navy is planning to use the nuclear-powered U.S.S. Gerald R. Ford to provide electricity to Naval Station Norfolk. This arrangement will leverage the Ford-class carrier's nuclear power system to support the Virginia facility.

The Navy aims to enhance energy resilience and ensure mission assurance at Naval Station Norfolk, one of the world's largest naval installations. The nuclear carrier will serve as a reliable power source for the base.

cards.headline: Texas Senate race tests staying power of anti-progressive messaging
cards.teaser: The Texas Senate race has become a testing ground for whether culture war politics still resonate with voters.
cards.body:
Republicans are testing anti-progressive messaging in the Texas Senate race ahead of the 2026 midterms. Shortly after winning the GOP primary runoff, Ken Paxton attacked Democratic nominee state Rep. James Talarico, calling him "too low-T for Texas" and making manhood a central issue in the race.

The contest has become a national laboratory for anti-"woke" politics, examining whether voters will continue responding to cultural messaging from 2020 and 2024, even as economic concerns weigh on the midterm environment.

cards.headline: Trump defends Lincoln Memorial pool renovation
cards.teaser: President Trump defended his administration's work on the Reflecting Pool in response to media criticism.
cards.body:
President Trump defended renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Friday, criticizing media coverage of the project. Trump described the pool's prior condition harshly, calling it "a disgusting, garbage strewn dump."

In his defense of the renovation work, Trump stated that professionals were now doing the right work for the project. He specifically targeted news outlets, including The New York Times, for their critical coverage of the renovations.

cards.teaser: The Ultimate Fighting Championship will hold a prime-time event at the White House next month.

cards.headline: States push to limit classroom technology and AI use
cards.teaser: At least 16 states have introduced bills to restrict technology use in schools.
cards.body:
Parents, educators and lawmakers are pushing schools to reduce classroom screen time amid concerns about student attention, behavior and learning. School cellphone bans are expanding into broader efforts to limit screen use and establish guardrails around AI in education.

At least 16 states have introduced bills to limit classroom technology. A nonprofit called Schools Beyond Screens formed last year with fewer than a dozen parents in Los Angeles but has since grown into a broader movement.
